speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and are they getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the progression over months with specific involvement of gait, bladder control, and speech is concerning. Can you tell me if you are experiencing any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs or hands, and have you noticed any changes in your balance or coordination?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.
